# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first portrait browser survival-evasion game titled "Elm Street: Dream Debt" from this brief: preserve a first-person tap-defense loop where enemies spawn at depth, advance toward the player, can be tapped/clicked to score, damage health on contact, and can be pushed back by holding a large action button or shaking the device. Express the whole loop as Nightmare on Elm Street dream-horror. A Nightmare on Elm Street dream-horror game with Freddy Krueger nightmare logic, surreal traps, sleep deprivation panic, dark comedy menace, and reality-bending supernatural dread with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range. Use vanilla Canvas/DOM, procedural horror art, readable HUD cards, large touch controls, optional camera fallback, non-blocking procedural audio, and clear start/game-over/restart states.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Truth
- genre: mobile-first first-person survival evasion / tap-defense arcade loop
- objective: survive as long as possible by tapping approaching hostile entities before contact and using run/shake input to buy distance
- input model: tap/click canvas to attack, hold a large bottom button to retreat, optional device motion shake to add retreat energy, start/restart buttons by native click/tap
- core loop: boot menu -> start -> optional camera/fallback scene -> timed enemy spawns -> enemies advance in depth -> player taps hitboxes to remove enemies and score -> contact removes health -> health zero opens game-over/restart
- fail/friction state: each close contact subtracts 20 health; at 0 health active play stops and final score is shown

## Protected Mechanics
- Spawn interval begins at 2000ms and tightens by score, capped at 500ms. Enemy depth movement, tap hitbox removal, score increment, health damage, retreat from hold-run/shake, and restart semantics are preserved.

## Transformable Surfaces
HUD copy, title, background drawing, enemy silhouette, weapon/feedback art, color system, atmospheric particles, optional GIF feedback, procedural scene motifs, and explanatory rules are presentation-only and safe to transform.
